name: Mary Wollstonecraft
worldviewSummary: Wollstonecraft argues that women are rational beings whose apparent inferiority results from a deficient education that trains them for pleasing rather than for reason and virtue. Rights and duties grounded in reason belong to all; dependence corrupts both the dependent and those who rule them.
biography: English writer, educator and philosopher. She wrote A Vindication of the Rights of Men (1790) in reply to Edmund Burke and A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792). She died shortly after giving birth to Mary Shelley.

works.title: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
A Vindication of the Rights of Men

concepts.description: Virtue requires the exercise of reason; denying women a rational education makes them dependent and then blames them for the weakness this produces.
Dependence on another's will — whether of women on men or subjects on hereditary privilege — degrades character.

positions.statement: Women should receive the same rational education as men, including co-educational national day schools, so that they can become independent and virtuous citizens.
She criticizes Rousseau's Emile for educating Sophie to please men, arguing this produces artificial weakness rather than virtue.
Virtue has one standard for both sexes; if women are moral agents they must be allowed to develop and exercise reason.

relations.note: Chapter 5 of the Vindication criticizes Rousseau's views on women's education.
